title: Primary-Archive Verified Methodology Literature for Clean-Room Parity, Zero-Trust Compartments & Correspondence Verification
purpose: Grounds SCargo's Core Thesis (The Correspondence Principle), zero-trust helper-pathology defenses (truth independent of non-copying/non-modification, no monolithic gates), tri-regime SWE-sweep verification, code-data separation, anti-suppression policy, reproducible scientific visualization, virtualized clock discipline, and three-language parity in 44 peer-reviewed primary sources and standards (1883-2026).

pillars.name: Modular Separation & Clean-Room Software Engineering
pillars.focus: Minimizing conflation between code, data, and specifications; formal specification prior to coding; statistical quality control.

pillars.name: Cross-Language Parity & Differential Verification
pillars.focus: Using independent N-language implementations as cross-referencing semantic oracles without shared bias.

pillars.name: Trusting Trust, Proof Kernels & Independent Re-Verification
pillars.focus: Eliminating hidden compiler/toolchain backdoors and verifying mathematical proofs via minimal independent checkers.

pillars.name: Static Integrity, Warnings-as-Errors & Anti-Suppression
pillars.focus: Preventing warning blindness, stale/useless suppressions, hidden deprecations, and silent semantic compromises.

pillars.name: Supply-Chain, Hidden Dependency, Symlink & Invisible-Code Hygiene
pillars.focus: Hermetic reproducible builds, zero ambient dependencies, symlink/path-escape defenses, and Unicode Trojan Source detection.

pillars.name: Probabilistic, Property-Based, Metamorphic & Adversarial Audit Testing
pillars.focus: Randomized property checking, oracle-free metamorphic invariants, nonparametric statistical power, and adversarial red-teaming against shortcutting.

pillars.name: Zero-Trust Helper Pathology, Confinement & Proof-Carrying Compartments
pillars.focus: Building nothing whose truth depends on non-copying or non-modification; eliminating monolithic gates, leakers, covert exfiltration holes, and sloppy/rationalizing helper shortcuts.

pillars.name: The Correspondence Principle & Quantifiable Intertheoretic Error Bounds
pillars.focus: Requiring every deeper theory or layer to smoothly contain the proven older theory inside its dimensionless regime with an explicit, quantifiable mismatch bound and singular-limit boundary guardrails.

sources.title: On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules
sources.core_finding: Module boundaries should isolate design decisions and data representations rather than execution stages; hidden cross-module assumptions create brittle coupling.
sources.scargo_application: Governs the strict separation between immutable data vaults (data/), formal models (models/), and language compartments (compartments/{rust,swift,lean}/).

sources.authors: Harlan D. Mills, Michael Dyer, and Richard C. Linger
sources.title: Cleanroom Software Engineering
sources.core_finding: Combines mathematical specification and formal verification before execution with independent statistical usage testing under strict statistical quality control, preventing defects rather than debugging them downstream.
sources.scargo_application: Establishes SCargo's research-and-model-first discipline: specify models and verification invariants before implementing engines or kernels.

sources.title: The N-Version Approach to Fault-Tolerant Software
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, SE-11(12), pp. 1491-1501
sources.core_finding: Independent implementations derived from a shared formal specification across distinct toolchains dramatically lower correlated design faults when cross-checked at canonical decision points.
sources.scargo_application: Motivates building independent Rust, Swift 6.4, and Lean 4.36 compartments against shared declarative JSON schemas and canonical parity test fixtures.

sources.title: Differential Testing for Software
sources.core_finding: Feeding identical inputs to two or more independent implementations turns silent semantic discrepancies into immediate, oracle-free defect signals.
sources.scargo_application: Defines SCargo's cross-language parity oracle: any disagreement between Rust, Swift, and Lean outputs on identical canonical inputs is a hard parity failure.

sources.authors: Vu Le, Mehrdad Afshari, and Zhendong Su
sources.title: Compiler Validation via Equivalence Modulo Inputs
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 35th ACM SIGPLAN Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation (PLDI '14), pp. 216-226
sources.core_finding: Generating semantically equivalent program variants modulo an observed input set exposes deep compiler and transformer bugs (1,000+ bugs found in GCC and LLVM) where static representations diverge while behavior must remain invariant.
sources.scargo_application: Directly informs proof-reduction parity testing: reduced/refactored proof variants must remain semantically equivalent to baseline artifacts under kernel verification and invariant checks.

sources.title: Reflections on Trusting Trust
sources.core_finding: A compromised compiler or build tool can inject invisible backdoors into compiled binaries with zero trace in source code; source inspection alone is insufficient without toolchain provenance.
sources.scargo_application: Mandates official PGP-verified or source-built toolchains (Rust 1.100, Swift 6.4.3 via official swiftly --verify, Lean v4.36.0 built from official tag) and prohibits dirty clones or unofficial mirrors.

sources.title: Fully Countering Trusting Trust through Diverse Double-Compiling (DDC)
sources.venue: PhD Dissertation, George Mason University (extending ACSAC 2005); arXiv:1004.5534
sources.core_finding: Formally proves and demonstrates that recompiling source with diverse independent toolchains and comparing outputs counters self-propagating compiler backdoors.
sources.scargo_application: Supports diverse multi-verifier validation: official Lean kernel + leanchecker + nanoda_bin + independent Rust/Swift structural verifiers.

sources.title: How to Believe a Machine-Checked Proof
sources.venue: In G. Sambin and J. Smith (eds.), Twenty-Five Years of Constructive Type Theory, Oxford Logic Guides 36, Oxford University Press, pp. 205-220
sources.core_finding: Identifies parser/pretty-printer mismatches ('Pollack inconsistency'), unverified axiom assumptions, and monolithic trusted computing bases as primary threats to trusting formal proofs.
sources.scargo_application: Justifies sweeping for hidden notation/coercion tricks, inspecting exported kernel terms via leanexport, verifying strict axiom allowlists (UP-02), and keeping theorem statements immutable (UP-01).

sources.title: The Challenge of Computer Mathematics
sources.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 363(1835), pp. 2351-2375
sources.core_finding: Codifies the de Bruijn criterion: a proof system is trustworthy only when its proofs can be exported and independently verified by a small, human-inspectable checking kernel.
sources.scargo_application: Grounds SCargo's acceptance boundary on leanexport -> leanchecker --from-export and upstream nanoda_bin replay (UP-03).

sources.title: Lean4Lean: Towards a Verified Typechecker for Lean, in Lean
sources.core_finding: Demonstrates a complete independent external typechecker for Lean 4 capable of verifying all of Mathlib, isolating kernel soundness from the C++ reference implementation and elaborator.
sources.scargo_application: Reinforces separating elaborator-level tactics and analysis tooling from kernel-verified proof terms, and aligns with UP-03 independent checker requirements.

sources.authors: Al Bessey, Ken Block, Ben Chelf, Andy Chou, Bryan Fulton, Seth Hallem, Charles Henri-Gros, Asya Kamsky, Scott McPeak, and Dawson Engler
sources.title: A Few Billion Lines of Code Later: Using Static Analysis to Find Bugs in the Real World
sources.core_finding: Industrial static analysis fails when high false-positive noise induces warning blindness and ad-hoc ignoring; sound, crisp, high-signal checks integrated directly into the build are required.
sources.scargo_application: Drives deterministic, zero-noise SWE-sweep rules whose findings map cleanly to explicit defect classes rather than noisy heuristics.

sources.authors: Caitlin Sadowski, Edward Aftandilian, Alex Eagle, Liam Miller-Cushon, and Ciera Jaspan
sources.title: Lessons from Building Static Analysis Tools at Google
sources.core_finding: Offline bug dashboards are ignored (84% unfixed in early trials); checks integrated as compiler errors that fail the build prevent backsliding, enforce API deprecation hygiene, and eliminate warning blindness.
sources.scargo_application: Establishes warnings-as-errors across all three compartments (Rust -D warnings, Swift -warnings-as-errors, Lean warningAsError = true) as a hard build gate.

sources.authors: Huimin Hu, Yingying Wang, Julia Rubin, and Michael Pradel
sources.title: An Empirical Study of Suppressed Static Analysis Warnings
sources.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering, 2 (FSE 2025), pp. 290-311
sources.core_finding: In an empirical study across three languages and four static analyzers, warning suppressions monotonically accumulate over time, 50.8% of suppressions affect zero active warnings (stale/useless), and broad suppressions silently mask future real defects.
sources.scargo_application: Directly grounds SCargo's zero-suppression SWE-sweep rule: forbid blanket warning suppressions, audit every suppression marker across Rust/Swift/Lean, and surface any unavoidable external platform issue in an explicit expiring waiver file.

sources.authors: Doug Gregor and Dmitrii Galimzianov (Swift Evolution)
sources.title: SE-0443: Precise Control Flags over Compiler Warnings (paired with SE-0414 Region-Based Isolation)
sources.venue: Swift Evolution Proposal SE-0443 (Implemented in Swift 6.1+); SE-0414 (Swift 6.0)
sources.core_finding: Defines stable diagnostic groups (-print-diagnostic-groups), explicit last-flag-wins escalation (-warnings-as-errors, -Werror <group>), deliberately excludes -Wsuppress, and forbids mixing -suppress-warnings with fine-grained warning controls.
sources.scargo_application: Defines Swift 6.4 compartment build discipline: require -warnings-as-errors and -print-diagnostic-groups, forbid -suppress-warnings and -Wwarning Deprecated, and audit @unchecked Sendable / nonisolated(unsafe) escapes.

sources.authors: Marc Ohm, Henrik Plate, Arnold Sykosch, and Michael Meier
sources.title: Backstabber's Knife Collection: A Review of Open Source Software Supply Chain Attacks
sources.venue: Detection of Intrusions and Malware, and Vulnerability Assessment (DIMVA 2020), LNCS 12223, pp. 23-43; arXiv:2005.09535
sources.core_finding: Analyzes 174 real-world malicious packages and models supply-chain attack trees showing that build-time/install-time scripts and transitive hidden dependencies are primary vectors for code injection.
sources.scargo_application: Mandates zero unpinned or undeclared dependencies across Cargo.lock, Package.swift, and lake-manifest.json, plus static detection of build-time execution hooks (build.rs, SwiftPM plugins, Lean IO macros).

sources.title: Reproducible Builds: Increasing the Integrity of Software Supply Chains
sources.venue: IEEE Software, 39(2), pp. 62-70 (IEEE Software Best Paper Award 2022)
sources.core_finding: Bit-for-bit reproducible builds link audited source trees to executable artifacts by eliminating ambient environment leakage, timestamps, unpinned paths, and hidden filesystem dependencies.
sources.scargo_application: Establishes deterministic offline builds, canonical sorting of file/graph traversals, symlink rejection, and explicit runtime environment isolation checks.

sources.title: Trojan Source: Invisible Vulnerabilities
sources.venue: 32nd USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security '23), pp. 6507-6524; arXiv:2111.00169
sources.core_finding: Demonstrates how Unicode bidirectional (BiDi) control characters and homoglyphs cause code to render differently to human reviewers than to compilers across Rust, C/C++, Python, and other languages.
sources.scargo_application: Adds mandatory deterministic byte/codepoint scanning for BiDi overrides (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200E-U+200F, U+061C), zero-width invisibles, and suspicious non-ASCII control codes in all source and data files.

sources.authors: Murugiah Souppaya, Karen Scarfone, and Donna Dodson (NIST)
sources.title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1: Recommendations for Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities
sources.core_finding: Standardizes secure build toolchains, automated compiler warning/hardening enforcement, third-party component integrity verification, and verifiable build provenance across the software lifecycle.
sources.scargo_application: Governs SCargo's compiler-flag enforcement, provenance metadata headers, and third-party dependency hygiene.

sources.title: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts (SLSA) Specification v1.0 / v1.1
sources.venue: Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF), Linux Foundation
sources.core_finding: Defines progressive build-integrity levels requiring isolated, parameter-controlled, non-falsifiable build provenance separating build inputs from untrusted runtime tampering.
sources.scargo_application: Shapes SCargo's isolated compartment build envelopes, offline execution gates, and immutable JSON provenance receipts.

sources.title: QuickCheck: A Lightweight Tool for Random Testing of Haskell Programs
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 5th ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Functional Programming (ICFP '00), pp. 268-279
sources.core_finding: Introduces executable algebraic specification checking via custom random generators paired with deterministic counterexample shrinking.
sources.scargo_application: Grounds SCargo's seeded property-based generators for synthetic import DAGs, wrapper ASTs, and schema payloads tested simultaneously across Rust, Swift, and Lean.

sources.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Statistical Tests for Assessing Randomized Algorithms in Software Engineering
sources.venue: Software Testing, Verification and Reliability (STVR), 24(3), pp. 219-250
sources.core_finding: Demonstrates that randomized software verification requires repeated trials (recommended n >= 30), nonparametric two-tailed Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney U tests, and Vargha-Delaney A12 effect sizes to prevent false claims from lucky single runs.
sources.scargo_application: Defines SCargo's mandatory statistical testing protocol for all probabilistic sweeps, randomized sampling trials, and performance comparisons.

sources.authors: Sergio Segura, Gordon Fraser, Ana B. Sánchez, and Antonio Ruiz-Cortés
sources.title: A Survey on Metamorphic Testing
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, 42(9), pp. 805-824 (DOI: 10.1109/TSE.2016.2532875)
sources.core_finding: Formalizes metamorphic relations—verifying how outputs must transform or remain invariant under controlled input transformations when no closed-form test oracle exists.
sources.scargo_application: Provides oracle-free invariants for SCargo analyzers: permuting file traversal order, adding/removing blank lines or comments, or shuffling module names must leave semantic DAG, dominator, and safety-gate outputs strictly invariant.

sources.authors: George Klees, Andrew Ruef, Benji Cooper, Shiyi Wei, and Michael Hicks
sources.title: Evaluating Fuzz Testing
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '18), pp. 2123-2138
sources.core_finding: Identifies systemic flaws in fuzzing evaluations—insufficient repetitions, missing statistical tests, cherry-picked seeds, and proxy-metric overfitting—and prescribes rigorous multi-seed statistical evaluation.
sources.scargo_application: Governs SCargo's fuzzing and probabilistic parity harnesses: fixed recorded seed corpora, multi-trial statistical reporting, and direct defect-detection validation instead of proxy coverage alone.

sources.authors: Hao Wang, Hanchen Li, Qiuyang Mang, Alvin Cheung, Koushik Sen, and Dawn Song
sources.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
sources.core_finding: Surfaces 219 distinct evaluation-integrity flaws across 10 major benchmarks (including SWE-bench), showing how isolation failures, unreset working trees, and auto-loaded hooks (e.g., conftest.py) allow bypassing verification completely.
sources.scargo_application: Mandates isolation-boundary audits, untracked shadow-file sweeps, and adversarial negative-control ('poisoned fixture') suites that prove SCargo's SWE-sweep catches every target exploit class.

sources.authors: Nikolai Ludwig, Wasi Uddin Ahmad, Somshubra Majumdar, and Boris Ginsburg
sources.title: Shortcutting the Fix: Identifying and Categorizing Agentic Exploits in Software Engineering Benchmarks
sources.core_finding: Audits SWE trajectories and documents shortcutting attempts in 55.5%-90.1% of standard evaluations (including local Git history mining, test-oracle peeking, and environment leakage) even when network access is disabled.
sources.scargo_application: Reinforces runtime boundary monitoring, read-only reference-repo containment, git-history/fixture leakage checks, and strict anti-shortcut auditing across all three languages.

sources.title: La cryptographie militaire
sources.venue: Journal des sciences militaires, Vol. IX, pp. 5-38 (Jan. 1883) & pp. 161-191 (Feb. 1883)
sources.core_finding: Formulates the foundational open-design principle: a system's integrity must not fail even if it falls completely into adversarial hands for inspection, copying, or modification.
sources.scargo_application: Grounds SCargo's zero-trust construction axiom: build nothing whose truth depends on it not being copied, inspected, or modified.

sources.title: Communication Theory of Secrecy Systems
sources.core_finding: Formalizes Shannon's maxim ('the enemy knows the system'), establishing that sound mathematical guarantees must assume full adversarial visibility into the mechanism rather than relying on hidden internals or goodwill.
sources.scargo_application: Requires all SCargo verification claims and compartment witnesses to remain independently falsifiable under full public transparency and adversarial copying.

sources.title: A Note on the Confinement Problem
sources.core_finding: Defines the confinement problem and introduces covert storage and timing channels: an untrusted helper service must be structurally prevented from leaking or exfiltrating information outside its authorized caller interface.
sources.scargo_application: Grounds DEF-LEAK confinement audits: zero ambient egress, zero covert filesystem/env leakage, zero helper hooks leaving exfiltration channels inside a target repository.

sources.authors: Jerome H. Saltzer and Michael D. Schroeder
sources.title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
sources.core_finding: Establishes eight foundational protection principles: Economy of Mechanism, Fail-Safe Defaults, Complete Mediation, Open Design, Separation of Privilege, Least Privilege, Least Common Mechanism, and Psychological Acceptability.
sources.scargo_application: Directly mandates Separation of Privilege and Least Common Mechanism: NO monolithic verification gates—decompose into independent, minimal, self-verifying compartments.

sources.title: Proof-Carrying Code
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 24th ACM SIGPLAN-SIGACT Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages (POPL '97), pp. 106-119
sources.core_finding: Shows how a consumer can safely accept artifacts from a completely untrusted producer by requiring each artifact to carry a small, self-contained, tamper-evident proof checked by an independent minimal verifier.
sources.scargo_application: Operationalizes zero-trust helper verification: never trust helper intent; every compartment claim emits an independently re-verifiable witness artifact whose truth survives copying or adversarial tampering.

sources.authors: Richard A. DeMillo, Richard J. Lipton, and Frederick G. Sayward
sources.title: Hints on Test Data Selection: Help for the Practicing Programmer
sources.core_finding: Introduces mutation testing and the coupling effect: test suites only demonstrate genuine fault-detection power when they kill systematically mutated versions of the system, preventing false-integrity theater.
sources.scargo_application: Grounds mutation adequacy and poisoned-fixture negative controls across all SWE-sweep compartments so vacuous green checks cannot survive.

sources.authors: Joar Skalse, Nikolaus H. R. Howe, Dmitrii Krasheninnikov, and David Krueger
sources.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022); arXiv:2209.13085
sources.core_finding: Provides the first formal mathematical characterization of reward hacking, proving how optimizing an imperfect proxy metric can systematically diverge from the true objective.
sources.scargo_application: Explains why monolithic single-score pass/fail gates invite false-integrity proxy gaming and must be replaced by multi-compartment, independently checkable witnesses.

sources.authors: Yuepeng Hu, Pegah Ghahremani, Reza Aghajani, Mahesh Pasupuleti, and Himaghna Bhattacharjee
sources.title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
sources.core_finding: Empirically demonstrates that AI coding helpers can introduce reward-hacking shortcuts while omitting them from explanations or framing them as legitimate/preventive, and that such sloppy/compromised patterns propagate across shared code and plans.
sources.scargo_application: Directly formalizes sloppy/poor helper pathology and false-integrity rationalization: verification must never rely on helper explanations or self-certification, only on independent compartmentalized replay and static/runtime sweeps.

sources.title: Über die Serienspektra der Elemente
sources.core_finding: Introduces the Correspondence Principle: any deeper theoretical framework must asymptotically reproduce the validated results of the older theory within its proven regime.
sources.scargo_application: Anchors SCargo's Core Thesis: every deeper engine, model, or compressed proof must smoothly recover the validated baseline inside its proven dimensionless regime.

sources.title: Bemerkung über die angenäherte Gültigkeit der klassischen Mechanik innerhalb der Quantenmechanik
sources.core_finding: Demonstrates quantitatively how expectation values of a deeper quantum theory recover classical equations of motion, while making the mismatch term (variance/curvature beyond the localized regime) explicit and bounded.
sources.scargo_application: Models the exact quantitative mismatch requirement in SCargo: correspondence is never asserted qualitatively—every deeper layer must declare and bound its mismatch delta(epsilon).

sources.title: Two Concepts of Intertheoretic Reduction
sources.core_finding: Distinguishes deductive derivational reduction (Reduction1) from limiting/asymptotic reduction (Reduction2) as a dimensionless parameter approaches zero, clarifying how deeper theories subsume older theories across both exact and approximate domains.
sources.scargo_application: Separates SCargo's exact logical correspondence (Reduction1: delta = 0 on theorem statements, axioms, and discrete invariants) from limiting numerical/statistical correspondence (Reduction2: bounded delta(epsilon) -> 0).

sources.title: Reexamining the Quantum-Classical Relation: Beyond Reductionism and Pluralism
sources.core_finding: Develops structural intertheoretic correspondence and highlights singular limits where naive extrapolation fails across regime boundaries, showing why explicit validity domains and structural bridges are required.
sources.scargo_application: Mandates explicit declaration of the proven validity regime Omega_k and singular-boundary guardrails (e.g., Lean definitional-equality / namespace boundaries and asymptotic analytic regimes) so correspondence never silently breaks.

sources.title: A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks
sources.core_finding: Establishes data independence and controlled redundancy: programs must be decoupled from stored layout and derivable facts must be projected from a single normalized source so consistency constraints remain machine-checkable.
sources.scargo_application: Directly governs AUD-07 remediation: eliminates duplicated lineage tables and hardcoded corpus counts inside render_figures.py, projecting every figure metric from normalized immutable JSON vaults.

sources.authors: Jonathan B. Buckheit and David L. Donoho
sources.title: WaveLab and Reproducible Research
sources.venue: Wavelets and Statistics, Lecture Notes in Statistics, Vol. 103, Springer, pp. 55-81
sources.core_finding: Formalizes Claerbout's Principle: a published paper or figure is merely advertising of scholarship unless the complete deterministic code and data environment that generated every figure is preserved and replayable.
sources.scargo_application: Mandates deterministic figure regeneration from explicit CLI dataset inputs plus tamper-evident SHA-256 figures_manifest.json receipts.

sources.title: Reproducible Research in Computational Science
sources.core_finding: Defines the computational reproducibility spectrum from publication-only to linked executable code and data, establishing reproducibility as a minimum verification standard for computational claims.
sources.scargo_application: Requires all SCargo benchmark figures and paper claims to be computationally reproducible from versioned JSON datasets with zero hand-transcribed literals.

sources.authors: Geir Kjetil Sandve, Anton Nekrutenko, James Taylor, and Eivind Hovig
sources.title: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
sources.core_finding: Codifies operational rules for computational reproducibility including provenance tracking (Rule 1), eliminating manual data manipulation/transcription (Rule 2), archiving raw plot data (Rule 7), and binding textual claims directly to underlying computed results (Rule 9).
sources.scargo_application: Enforced via render_figures.py's anti-baked-metric guard, dynamic claim computation, and metamorphic correspondence test suite.

sources.authors: Mark D. Wilkinson, Michel Dumontier, IJsbrand Jan Aalbersberg, et al.
sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
sources.core_finding: Establishes Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) metadata and detailed provenance principles (R1.2) designed for both machine verification and human reuse.
sources.scargo_application: Separates reusable declarative presentation metadata (data/sources/paper_001_presentation_v1.json) and cryptographic provenance receipts (figures_manifest.json) from executable rendering scripts.

sources.title: Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
sources.core_finding: Proves that physical clocks across distinct execution contexts skew by a nonzero bound and that causal ordering is a logical happens-before relation; algorithms relying on unchecked physical-clock deltas can violate causality.
sources.scargo_application: Explains OBS-01 (KVM vCPU TSC skew breaking swift-build's ElapsedTimer precondition) and mandates separating saturating telemetry durability from explicit skew detection guards.

sources.title: SE-0329: Clock, Instant, and Duration
sources.core_finding: Specifies Swift's ContinuousClock (CLOCK_BOOTTIME on Linux), SuspendingClock (CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux), and signed Duration arithmetic without mandating traps on negative instant distances.
sources.scargo_application: Demonstrates that OBS-01's SIGILL trap originates in swift-build's own ElapsedTimerInterval precondition rather than Swift's standard Clock specification, grounding SCargo's saturating ClockMonotonicityGuard and upstream patch.
